summary: In this excerpt from a novel, Mrs. Royce tells Lexy Moran about a young woman who lives isolated three miles from the village of Wyngate and whom she saw only once, nearly three years earlier, when Dr. Quelton brought her there as a bride during a snowstorm. Mrs. Royce claims the doctor is crazy, a view she says others share. Dr. Quelton then enters with Captain Grey, who is unconcerned by the gossip and offers to visit the isolated house himself, planning to return for lunch.
one_line: Mrs. Royce gossips to Lexy Moran about a reclusive young bride and her supposedly crazy doctor husband, Dr. Quelton, near Wyngate.
key_facts: Mrs. Royce says the young woman lives out in a lonely place and never sees a soul from one month's end to another.
Mrs. Royce describes the young woman as young and as pretty as a picture.
Mrs. Royce saw the young woman the night the doctor brought her to Wyngate as a young bride.
The arrival took place about three years before the conversation, during a terrible snowstorm.
The young woman sat in the same room in Wyngate where Lexy is sitting.
The young woman lives only three miles from Wyngate, and Mrs. Royce has never seen her again.
Mrs. Royce says that Dr. Quelton is crazy and that she is not the only one to say so.
Dr. Quelton enters the room with a very nice smile and says he is sorry he did not wait longer for Miss Moran.
Dr. Quelton went out to telephone to tell Muriel he was there, but the house has no telephone.
Lexy says she does not think Dr. Quelton is a real doctor, meaning a physician.
Lexy tells Captain Grey that Mrs. Royce says Dr. Quelton is crazy.
Captain Grey suppresses a smile and says that in little villages anyone out of the ordinary is called crazy.
Captain Grey proposes to walk three miles to pay a call and return to Wyngate for lunch.
Captain Grey says Lexy had said she would let him help her in her little project.
